title: The Hollow Gravity
premise: August Reyes, a clone of a murdered freighter captain, has spent ten years hauling cargo through contested orbits, keeping his head down and his lineage secret. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream—a signal bleeding through from the relay at the edge of dead space—August realizes it's a distress call tied to the original's unsolved murder and to something buried in the relay itself. Hunted by corporate agents who want the signal silenced and betrayed by the one ally he trusted with the truth, August must race a dying ship and a closing jump window to reach the relay. He arrives to find the original's killer waiting among the relay's caretakers, exposes the conspiracy that murdered him, and chooses to broadcast the truth at the cost of his own anonymity—finally belonging not as a copy, but as himself.
about_author: Quentin Eastwick is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. They live near a decommissioned tracking station and write stories about people who inherit other people's ghosts.

chapters.title: Manifest Weight
chapters.summary: POV: August. Ten years after inheriting the original Reyes's murder case and identity debts, August hauls contraband water ice through contested orbits, invisible by design. A routine inspection nearly exposes his clone status. Emotional beat: weary vigilance—the cost of staying unseen.

chapters.title: The Children's Frequency
chapters.summary: POV: Mara, a colony schoolteacher. Children across three habitats wake reciting the same coordinates in their sleep. Officials dismiss it as mass hysteria; Mara recognizes the numbers match a dead-space relay chart. She brings the data to August, the only pilot who flies that route. Emotional beat: unease curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Logbook
chapters.summary: POV: August. Cross-referencing the dream coordinates with the original's sealed logbook, August finds encrypted entries suggesting the original discovered something at the relay—and was killed for it. His old friend Dov, a station engineer, offers help decoding. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Contract of Silence
chapters.summary: POV: August. Corporate liaison Vess Karrow offers August a lucrative contract contingent on handing over the logbook and reporting anyone who asks about the dreams. Refusal means blacklisting. August pretends to accept while planning escape. Emotional beat: moral compromise tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: What Dov Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. Mara discovers Dov has been feeding the children's dream data to Karrow for months—he sold out the colony to protect his family's residency permits. Confronting him shatters August's last trust. Emotional beat: betrayal; loyalty revealed as transactional.

chapters.title: Burn for the Edge
chapters.summary: POV: August. With Karrow's enforcers raiding the docks, August launches early on a half-fueled ship, taking Mara and two of the dreaming children as living receivers. The jump window to dead space closes in nine days. Emotional beat: desperate commitment—no way back.

chapters.title: Dead Space Lessons
chapters.summary: POV: Ila, age eleven, the strongest receiver. In transit, the children's dream sharpens into instructions: the relay is a listening post, and the original recorded proof of a corporate massacre there. Ila begins channeling fragments aloud. Emotional beat: wonder and terror entwined.

chapters.title: The Caretaker
chapters.summary: POV: August. Arriving at the derelict relay, they find its lone caretaker: Sef, the original's former partner, presumed dead—the actual murderer, hiding where no warrant reaches. Sef claims he killed to bury the massacre evidence and save thousands of colonists' contracts. Emotional beat: confrontation with the man who made August possible.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: POV: August. Karrow's ship arrives, forcing a standoff inside the relay. Sef tries to destroy the archive; August must choose between killing him and trusting him long enough to transmit. The children hold the frequency open as the window narrows to minutes. Emotional beat: climax—truth versus survival, decided in seconds.

chapters.title: Signal, Received
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. The broadcast goes out; the massacre evidence reaches every colony before Karrow can jam it. Sef surrenders to the arriving colonial tribunal; August, exposed as a clone, is met not with revulsion but with recognition. Back home, the children stop dreaming. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging earned by standing visible.
